column2: What is missing from my genealogy, and where should I look for it?
column3: Research → Type of research → “🔍 What’s missing?”. For each ancestor in the line (up to 12 generations): the missing birth, marriage, death or parents, but also censuses (1836-1936), the military register (men born from 1847 to 1921), the estate and the marriage contract; with the commune, the window of years, the archive service (Departmental Archives of such-and-such department, according to the place) and the series to consult according to the period: parish registers before 1792, civil registration and ten-year indexes afterwards, notaries (3 E), registration (3 Q), recruitment (1 R), censuses (6 M). Sort by archive service, commune, ancestor or kind of record; “📌 To tracking” adds the search “to do” in the Archive record index, and what is already there is shown. “🖨 Print” makes the list for a visit to the archives.

column2: How do I extract an ancestor’s signature or create a monogram, a wax seal?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → “🔤 Signatures and seals”. ✍️ Choose the image of a record (media or computer), frame the signature by dragging: yellowed paper, stains and the lines of the register disappear (threshold set automatically, to fine-tune), the ink becomes a clean vector line, in its original colour or a chosen ink; the cut-out image (transparent background) can also go into the person’s media. 🔏 For a monogram: interlaced initials (copperplate, round hand, Gothic, Roman capitals, Didot), in a wax seal, an ink stamp, a medallion, a shield, a lozenge or a bookplate, with a legend going around it (“MARTIN FAMILY · TULLE 1832”). Everything opens in the vector drawing to be retouched, printed or exported.

column2: Page layout: how do I see whether text overflows and make it continue in another box?
column3: At the bottom of the page layout, an indicator: 🟢 “No errors”, or 🔴 with the number of errors (text overflowing its box, fact contradicted by the records). It updates by itself while you write; a click opens the detailed check with “Go” for each problem. A box whose text overflows has a small red + at the bottom right: click it, then click the text box that should receive the rest (on any page) — the text continues there, as in InDesign. Also: Object → “➜ Thread the text box to another…”, “⤵ Flow the text onto new pages” and “Break the thread”. Esc cancels.

column2: Page layout: is the text of a book checked against the records?
column3: Yes. When a text names a person in the database (“Jean MARTIN, born on 28 August 1923 in Tulle”), the date and place of birth, baptism, death, burial or marriage are compared with their record. A different date counts as an error (🔴), a different place (even without a date: “born in Tulle” while the record says Naves) or a name carried by several records as “to check” (🟠), and a fact missing from the record is pointed out so you can add it. “He” or “she” refer to the person named just before; the “date Birth — place” lines of a record page refer to the name in the title. Nothing is changed automatically: you correct the text or the record. The details are in File → “✅ Check before printing” (or a click on the indicator).

column2: How do I write text that follows a circle or a curve?
column3: Vector drawing → Object → “➰ Text on a curve…”: circle, arc, wave, the chosen path, or the templates “motto around a seal” and “name on a ribbon”. In Properties → Text: position on the path, offset, side (underneath to write the right way round at the bottom of a circle), spread the letters. The shape is changed with Direct selection (A).

column2: How do I print a coat of arms in black and white (heraldic hatching)?
column3: Coat of arms mode → “🖨 Heraldic hatching”: or = dots, argent = plain, gules = vertical lines, azure = horizontal, vert = diagonals from dexter, sable = cross-hatching, purpure = diagonals from sinister. “Back to colour” cancels; “＋ Legend” adds the table of hatchings.

column2: How do I make a gradient with several colours or hatching in a drawing?
column3: Properties → Colour → Kind of fill: linear or radial gradient (“＋ Add a colour”, position of each), or Pattern (hatching, dots, grid, cross-hatching, chequerboard).

column2: Where can I find fleurons, frames, corners, drop caps for a drawing?
column3: The “Ornaments” tab of the vector drawing: 44 old ornaments with search and categories; click to place in the centre, or drag onto the drawing. The Colour palette recolours them.

column2: How do I align or distribute objects in a drawing?
column3: Properties → Position and size: six alignment buttons and two to distribute, relative to the selection or to the artboard (the page, the panel). When moving, enlarging or drawing, pink lines snap to edges and centres; hold ⌘ (or Ctrl) to do without.

column2: How do I make a double-sided or folded announcement card, with its envelope?
column3: Announcement window → Folding (double-sided, folded in 2, 3 or 4 panels) and “✉️ Matching envelope” (size chosen automatically or as you like, recipient taken from the people, sender). In the drawing, the pink lines are the folds. ⤓ Export → PDF (one page per side) or “🗞 Double-sided on A4” (sides placed, crop and fold marks).

column2: Do I need to click “Save” in Settings?
column3: No: each change is saved straight away. “✓ Saved” appears to the right of the page title, and a message at the bottom left offers “↶ Undo” to go back on the last change. “↺ Reset to default”, always to the right of the title, puts back the original settings (and “↶ Undo” brings yours back).

column2: Where have the other buttons at the top of a page gone?
column3: At the top of each page: the main button in blue, two others at most, then “⋯” which opens the rest (Assemble photos, Retouch, Export…), and ⭐ to add it to your shortcuts. The small blue text above the title says where you are (e.g. “Lists · Media and documents”); the number of items is written under the search bar.

column2: How do I see a list as thumbnails?
column3: At the top of the list, “List | Cards”: in “Cards”, each item has the same thumbnail everywhere (image, name, two useful lines, badges, date), with “Open” and “⋯” for Edit, Rename, Duplicate or Delete. The choice is remembered for each list.

column2: How do I keep, export or import a saved setting?
column3: In a “💾 Saved settings” frame (click its title to open it): “＋ Save the current settings”, a name, then Enter. Each setting has “Apply” and a ⋯ menu: replace with the current settings, rename, duplicate, ⤓ export (lcnda-reglage-….json file), delete (with “↶ Undo”). On the other computer, “⤒ Import” at the bottom of the frame. A file from another tool is refused with a message; if the name already exists, the app asks for another one.

column2: How do I export a drawing, a page layout or a plan?
column3: “⤓ Export ▾” at the top of the tool always opens the same window: PDF, PNG, JPG, SVG, Print, the tool’s file (to reopen later), with the quality, bleed and crop marks, the file name and a copy in the media.

column2: How do I put a family tree in my book?
column3: In the page layout: Object → “🌳 Insert a family tree”. Choose the person, the shape (ancestors, descendants, hourglass or fan), the number of generations and the style of the boxes. The tree follows your database: it remakes itself on opening, or with File → “↻ Update the dynamic objects”.

column2: How do I add a footnote or cite a source in a book?
column3: Double-click in a text, place the cursor, then Text → “¹ Note” or “📚 Cite a source” (“AD Corrèze, 3 E 123, f° 12”). The numbers put themselves back in order. Document → Footnotes: at the bottom of the box or at the end of the chapter. Object → “Insert the bibliography” lists the sources cited.

column2: How do I make an index of places or occupations?
column3: In the page layout: Object → “📍 Insert an index of places” or “🔨 … of occupations”. The index looks for the places and occupations of your database in the text and notes the pages. You can also mark a word with the “Place to index” or “Occupation to index” style.

column2: How do I make an e-book (ePub)?
column3: Page layout → ⤓ Export → “📱 ePub”. The file opens in Books, Kobo or Calibre, with the cover, the table of contents, the images and the notes.

column2: How do I get a cousin to proofread my book?
column3: Choose some words or an object, then Review → “💬 Comment” or “✎ Suggest”. To send it: ⤓ Export → “💬 Review”. Your cousin imports the file into 📐 Page layout, comments and sends you theirs back; you do Review → “⤒ Import their comments”. Suggestions are accepted or refused in one click. The “📝 Annotated PDF” can be read on paper.

column2: What does the red indicator of the page layout check?
column3: Overflowing texts, dates and places that contradict the records, impossible dates (30 February), impossible or wrong ages (“died at 140”), misspelt names (“Jean MARTAIN” → MARTIN?), places unknown to your database and wrong Sosa numbers. Click the indicator to see the details.

column2: How does the app write a person’s biography?
column3: On the record, the “📖 Biography” block writes their life in French from what the record contains (“Jean naît le 3 mai 1832 à Tulle, fils de…”), without inventing anything, in the feminine or masculine, with “vers 1784” for an approximate date. Choose the length (Short, Normal, Detailed), the tone (Neutral, Warm) and, in “⚙️ What is included”, the occupations, the witnesses, the censuses and the sources (in brackets or as notes). “✎ Edit” then “💾 Keep my version”: your version is used everywhere (family book, page layout with the {biographie} field). “↻ Regenerate” shows what has changed (green: added, red struck through: removed). “Place in ▾” puts it into a Note, a book or a presentation.

column2: How do I tell “a day in the life” of an ancestor (⏳)?
column3: On their record, ⋯ → “⏳ A day in their life…” (or, in the “📖 Biography” block, the “⏳ A day…” button). Choose a day of their life (an event, or the shortcuts Birth, Marriage, Death…) or “✎ Another date” (“7 May 1925”, “12 Thermidor Year II”). The app writes a short story in French using only its own rules, without the Internet: their age, their family that day, their village (village page, recorded population, church, your notes), their occupation (dictionary of old occupations), the day of the week, the saint of the day, the Republican date, the weather of the past if the data is installed, the big events of the year and, only when a reliable figure exists, a price or a wage from the table supplied with the app. Each sentence has its mark: ✓ from the record (with “↗ See the event”), 📚 reference (source cited in the Landmarks), 💭 imagined (in italics); the “No imagined sentences” switch removes them. Then: 📋 Copy, 📝 In the word processor, 🔊 Read aloud, “Place in ▾” (page layout, media, end of their biography, with ↶ Undo). A confidential record does not leave the app; for a living person, the window says so.
